1.why: A is the confidence/accuracy dissociation that is the only claim in the set specific to flashbulb memory as a distinct category; B is illegal because a memory forgotten entirely within a few years cannot be the thing a passage is characterizing as a flashbulb memory, so it could not strengthen any such characterization.

2.why: B and D corroborate each other on 18 kg for the untreated plot and D gives the full monotonic rise to 44 kg; A (high dose lowest) and C (low and medium tied at 29) each contradict that corroborated 18-to-44 rise, so both are illegal against the same graph.

3.why: B is the only option that holds both sides (deliberate effect plus genuinely unfinished passages); A's 'entirely the product of external constraints' and D's 'proves Titian consciously anticipated modern painting' are both unqualified claims a passage stating a mixed account could not support.

4.why: C is direct on-floor evidence of warm-season-only occupation, the one option reporting evidence from the site itself; B is illegal because the quarry distance of the building stone answers a question about construction logistics, not about who occupied the structures or when.

5.why: B names the exact assumption a reconsolidation therapy rests on (that the reactivated trace is the original, permanently altered) and breaks it; A is illegal for a stem asking what would undermine, since a drug that reduces emotional charge for days after treatment is evidence for the proposal, not against it.

6.why: B is the hedged structural inference ('could fail to provide'); A is illegal on its universal quantifier ('faster than any heat-tolerant species could'), and C inverts the risk by making loss of the heat-TOLERANT colonies the threat, which no text contrasting tolerant with common symbionts would assert.

7.why: A is the only option stating a non-default economics (prestige from giving away); B, C and D all restate the ordinary accumulate-and-store view that would make the passage not worth writing, but none of them is illegal on the option set alone.

8.why: D is the accept-but-qualify relation; B is illegal because 'denying that printing played any role at all' is an absolute no second text framed as a response would occupy, and A's claim that the press DELAYED the Reformation is a reversal no 'relationship between the texts' stem in this set supports.

9.why: C is the hedged functional inference; A ('no measurable effect') and B ('physically unable ... even when circumstances require it') are both absolutes that a text observing a pitch difference between roadside and quiet-park birds could not license.

10.why: D is the only option giving a positive physical signature (wavelength-dependent extinction, i.e. dust), and A is its null foil; C is illegal because a slow decline across the whole observing run describes a different phenomenon than the discrete dimming events the stem's 'each dimming' presupposes.

11.why: B is the hedged interior state ('a pull toward change she does not act on openly') typical of a literary inference key; C is illegal because indifference to the shop's arrangement contradicts the premise of a stem asking what the text supports about her relation to it.

12.why: A is the no-mechanism objection; D is illegal on chronology, since seafloor spreading postdates Wegener's critics and cannot be why they rejected him, and B's 'refused on principle to weigh any evidence' is an absolute about motive that a text explaining a scientific objection would not assert.

13.why: C is the controlled comparison that removes the causal link between elk avoidance and willow recovery; D is illegal for an undermining stem because a halving of elk numbers is consistent with, and would tend to support, the landscape-of-fear account rather than weaken it.

14.why: A is the split verdict (insulation works for filaments, not for complex vaned feathers); C ('fundamentally mistaken, feathers show no genuine link to thermoregulation') and D ('irrelevant') are both flat rejections, and a text that merely limits a hypothesis cannot support characterizing it as having no genuine link at all.

15.why: B describes a two-move structure (familiar interpretation, then the event recast as a later construct); C is illegal because supplying a more accurate date is a different move than any option here describes, and D is illegal because 'the empire survive intact into the medieval period' overstates administrative continuity into a claim of survival.

16.why: C (gradual, deliberate abandonment) and D (single catastrophic winter) are direct contraries so at most one is legal, and C is the one that a stem about excavation evidence supports; B is a salvage detail, not a main idea, and A generalizes to medieval villages at large, beyond a single excavated site.

17.why: C is the qualified-support relation; D's 'fully confirms across every category of crime' is an absolute that no second text supplying evidence could establish, and A refutes Jacobs outright, which cannot coexist with a stem asking how the evidence relates rather than whether it overturns.

18.why: A is the constructed-in-retrospect reading that the scare quotes around 'lessons' in the stem set up; C is illegal because dismissing such lessons as self-deception is a stronger normative verdict than a text that merely locates their origin after the fact would deliver.

19.why: C and D make contradictory claims about the same table row (Cereal D at 10 g with the longest versus the shortest fullness duration), so at most one is legal; C is the one that supports rather than contradicts a fiber-to-fullness claim, and B likewise reports a counter-trend.

20.why: A and B corroborate each other on 21 g per 100 mL at 10 C with B giving the rise to 58 g at 70 C; C (identical 39 g at 30 C and 50 C) and D (a steady fall ending at 21 g at 70 C) both contradict that corroborated pair of endpoints.

21.why: A is the setup-for-the-author's-alternative purpose; B is illegal on 'entirely free of ideological isolation', an absolute no survey sentence establishes, and C is illegal because offline friendships answer a different question than a sentence surveying ONLINE behavior.

22.why: The stem's quotation marks around 'as equals' signal a qualification, and B supplies it; D is illegal because it takes the claim at face value against that framing, and C (excluding merchants and physicians in favor of the clergy) inverts the membership the claim of equality presupposes.

23.why: A names a comparison the passage would have had to run (fungal condition versus seed-source proximity); C is illegal because a passage reporting findings about recolonization contradicts the claim that soil scientists abandoned the topic, and D's 'permanently prevent any native species' is an absolute the same findings would refute.

24.why: D is the population-level functional claim about counterillumination; A is illegal because a replacement sequence over evolutionary time is a claim about origins that a passage contrasting two present-day functions does not make, and B's head-to-head 'draws prey more effectively' compares a concealment mechanism against a lure on the wrong axis.
